asr.full_text: This week has been quite strong for the altcoin market. It was mainly privacy tokens and storage-related tokens that rallied. But there was one token, the NEAR protocol, that also performed pretty well despite not being in those narratives. The question is why? How much longer can this rally last? Is this potential for further outperformance? Let's have a look at the data most people are not considering. So we are currently at a bit over three dollars we have appreciated by fifty percent last week and while there have been two major rallies for near protocol so in 2021 and 2024 the price tended to decline over time the market cap was relatively stable from peak to peak we turned around at around 10 billion dollars and currently we are only at 4 billion so is there the potential for another 100 maybe even 200 return from here because when we look at the relative valuation to bitcoin nia still seems to be very depressed yes the long-term chart isn't that great but we have seen a recent support and there is just according to this chart the potential of maybe 250 percent and in the very best case, more than 700%. But of course, that would bring the market cap to heights we have never seen in the past. Now, where does the disconnect between the price development and the market cap development come from? It, of course, comes from token inflation. More and more near tokens hit the market over time. And the early investors, the insiders and the team cash out. But pretty much all of those unlocks have already happened, now it's just epoch rewards that continue to expand the supply. And again, when a token becomes less inflationary, that's a potentially good sign for future outperformance. We can see here how the underperformance of NIR relative to other altcoins tended to diminish over time it has stabilized now this is near relative to the others market cap so how is near doing relative to other altcoins from this bottom to this bottom we saw an underperformance of 22% subsequently we again had a 22 percent underperformance but that time it took much longer and now we see even less under performance so you can clearly see the price appears to be stabilizing, which makes sense, given that the insiders aren't cashing out anymore. It's only supply growth through epoch rewards. Let's have a look at some on-chain metrics. There is a ported version of the Neer token on the Ethereum chain, and we've got a bit over 10,000 holders of that token on ETH. So to be more precise, it's ten thousand eight hundred seventy six wallets that hold the token on the Ethereum chain and on the left side, we see the number of wallets of at least 330 NEAR tokens. That's roughly $1,000 worth of the token. So the small retail investor continues to buy. In the middle, we've got the wallet of at least $10,000 worth of the token. It's also long term accumulation. On the right side we've got the number of whales so the number of wallets with at least a hundred thousand dollars worth of nia so it seems like the investor base continues to grow what about the usage of the blockchain itself is that growing as well the answer is unfortunately no this is the number of transactions on nir over time it peaked one and a half years ago and since then it's shrinking. Here's the number of unique accounts, this is also shrinking and here is the transaction fee chart which unfortunately spikes every now and then, so there is a bottlenecking of the blockchain when there is too much usage. I don't really like doing it but that's how the YouTube game works. That's how the algorithm works. Please give this video a like if what you've seen so far has been useful. Thank you very much. Here's the total value locked of NIR. So how much capital is currently on the chain measured in NIR tokens. This is actually growing quite nicely. Here's the stablecoin market cap over time, unfortunately also declining, but not all numbers look look bad. This is the app revenue and this is the Decentralized Exchange Trading Volume, which is now at an all time high, even measured in U.S. Dollars, not just measured in NEAR. In NEAR, the growth looks even steeper. So again, there is a case to be made that NEAR might be bottoming out over here that it could outperform the rest of the altcoin market because the supply doesn't grow as much anymore, and why the number of active addresses isn't growing the trading itself is So, the existing users are using the NEAR Chain more than before. Let's have a look at the levered bets on the price as we usually do on this channel. In the last 24 hours, we had 172 million worth of trading volume on binance on the spot market and on the perpetual futures market we had more than that so there is quite a bit of leverage in near as well roughly three times the trading volume on the levered bets on the price many people got wiped out on the 10th of october this is true for pretty much any altcoin many alts experience a flash crash on that day including near and since that flash crash the market makers tend to not buy enough of the supply anymore. So the funding rate isn't clearly positive as it used to be. It's now fluctuating around zero. The trading volume is neither elevated nor depressed. But unfortunately, the amounts of bets on the price, so the open interest is relatively high and that is a red flag because there is positive correlation between open interests. So that's in green and the spot price. Whenever there are some more bets on the price, then the spot price tends to be high. Whenever there are less bets on the price, spot price tends to be low. And since we currently see that many bets on NEAR, we do have above average risk in the asset. Yes, there is a lot of potential upside. We could clearly double and triple from here. $10 per year is definitely possible. But this is all under the assumption that the open interest won't go down in the near future.
